To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“We have engineered a plant that produces a novel compound with potential health benefits.”

1) the use of a combination of different metabolic engineering approaches (overexpression of genes, knockout of genes) resulted in an increased accumulation of the desired metabolite (in this case the phytochemicals) 2) this increased accumulation was achieved by increasing the metabolic flux towards the target phytochemicals, and 3) the increased metabolic flux was achieved by the overexpression of genes involved in the metabolic pathway of the target phytochemistry.

(1) we identified a set of enzymes and pathways for the biosynthesis of phytochemicals; (2) we demonstrated the potential of metabolic engineering to produce these phytochemicals in plants and microorganisms; and (3) we developed a platform to engineer the production of these phytochemical in plants, yeast, and bacteria.
